title: Compare a stated belief with an ordinary week

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A mismatch may require changing conduct, revising an overbroad belief or accepting a legitimate competing duty. Three moments are a sample, not an identity verdict. A later observation should test the adjustment rather than retell the intention.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Pat says “friendship means answering every message immediately.” Monday: a welcome 10-minute call occurred. Wednesday: a necessary care task delayed a reply until evening. Friday: Pat browsed optional videos and forgot a promised reply by 17:00. A friend agrees a Saturday 10:00 check-in would work; no broader reassurance is supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Classify reflected, conflicting and ambiguous moments. Decide which belief and which behavior need revision. Plan an inspectable Saturday adjustment before reading the check.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person says family matters most but declines an optional gathering to keep an urgent agreed care duty elsewhere. Must the belief be false?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Monday reflects friendship; Wednesday supports revising “immediately” to fit necessary care; Friday still contains a missed promise. Later fiction: the Saturday call occurs 10:00–10:10; trust repair is not reported. A sound adjustment combines realistic response agreements and a reminder for explicit promises. Partial: revise only the slogan. Incorrect: use Wednesday’s care duty to excuse Friday’s unrelated omission.
criteria: Different causes of mismatch are retained
Later action is separate from intention

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. The event has competing duties and may express a broader care commitment. Examine actual promises and alternatives before deciding whether belief or conduct needs revision; one event does not settle identity.
